  Install gulp-plugins-hub plugins and write a first gulp 5 gulpfile with
  pipeline, source maps and options validated up front.
---

# Getting started

gulp-plugins-hub is a set of gulp plugins, each in its own package, that share one way of working: typed options checked when the plugin is created, hooks that get the file, errors that name the plugin and the file.

## Requirements

* Node.js 22.13 or newer
* gulp 5 (gulp 4 works too)

## Install

Install gulp and the plugins the build needs:

```sh
npm install --save-dev gulp @zilero/gulp-scss-compiler @zilero/gulp-css-squeezer @zilero/gulp-js-squeezer
```

## A first gulpfile

```js
// gulpfile.mjs
import { dest, parallel, src } from 'gulp';
import { pipeline } from 'node:stream/promises';
import cssSqueezer from '@zilero/gulp-css-squeezer';
import jsSqueezer from '@zilero/gulp-js-squeezer';
import scssCompiler from '@zilero/gulp-scss-compiler';

export const styles = () =>
  pipeline(
    src('src/styles/*.scss', { sourcemaps: true }),
    scssCompiler(),
    cssSqueezer(),
    dest('dist/css', { sourcemaps: '.' })
  );

export const scripts = () =>
  pipeline(src('src/js/*.js', { sourcemaps: true }), jsSqueezer(), dest('dist/js', { sourcemaps: '.' }));

export default parallel(styles, scripts);
```

Tasks return `pipeline(…)` from `node:stream/promises` rather than a `.pipe()` chain, so an error in any step ends the task with that error ([why](/guide/gulp-5#return-pipeline-not-a-pipe-chain)).

```sh
npx gulp
```

Every plugin is a function that takes its options and returns a stream. Each has a default export and a named one:

```js
import scssCompiler from '@zilero/gulp-scss-compiler';
import { scssCompiler } from '@zilero/gulp-scss-compiler'; // the same function
```

In a CommonJS gulpfile, use the named export:

```js
// gulpfile.js
const { scssCompiler } = require('@zilero/gulp-scss-compiler');
```

## Options are checked up front

Every option is validated when the plugin is created. A wrong value stops the task before any file is read, and lists every problem:

```text
[10:42:01] 'styles' errored after 3 ms
[10:42:01] Error in plugin "@zilero/gulp-css-squeezer"
Message:
    Invalid options:
    • Unrecognized key: "minfy"
```

## Errors name the file

An error while processing a file is a `PluginError` emitted on the stream, with the plugin name and the file:

```text
[10:42:05] Error in plugin "@zilero/gulp-scss-compiler"
Message:
    Undefined variable.
    ╷
  3 │ .card { color: $brand; }
    │                ^^^^^^
    ╵
Details:
    fileName: /project/src/styles/main.scss
```

In a `watch` task an error stops that run; gulp keeps watching.

* [Recipes](/guide/recipes): incremental builds, responsive images, font subsets.

* [Troubleshooting](/guide/troubleshooting): corrupted images, CommonJS and TypeScript gulpfiles, native binaries in CI.
* [Plugins](/plugins/): every plugin and its options.

---
url: /gulp-plugins-hub/guide/gulp-5.md
description: >-
  The gulp 5 changes every build runs into: binary files and encoding false,
  glob order, source maps, pipeline, ES modules and TypeScript gulpfiles.
---

# Gulp 5 essentials

Gulp 5 changed a few defaults that every build runs into. The plugins handle them, but some need a setting in your gulpfile.

## Binary files need `encoding: false`

Gulp 5 reads every file as UTF-8 text. Images, fonts and other binary files come out corrupted: every byte that is not valid UTF-8 becomes `U+FFFD`. Read them with `encoding: false`:

```js
src('src/images/**', { encoding: false });
src('src/fonts/*.ttf', { encoding: false });
```

[image-squeezer](/plugins/image-squeezer) and [font-switcher](/plugins/font-switcher) recognize a file read as text and fail with this fix in the message, instead of a decoder error. Plugins that only copy or pack files ([archive-creator](/plugins/archive-creator), [folder-clone](/plugins/folder-clone), [asset-revision](/plugins/asset-revision)) cannot tell: read binary files with `encoding: false` there too, or the copies are corrupted.

## Glob order is not kept

Gulp 4 emitted the files of `src(['a/*.js', 'b/*.js'])` in the order of the globs. Gulp 5 does not. When order matters, set it in the plugin:

```js
src('src/js/**/*.js').pipe(fileConcat({ name: 'app.js', order: ['vendor/**', 'lib/**'] }));
```

## Source maps without gulp-sourcemaps

`src` and `dest` handle source maps themselves:

```js
src('src/**/*.scss', { sourcemaps: true }) // reads existing maps, starts empty ones
  .pipe(scssCompiler())
  .pipe(cssSqueezer())
  .pipe(dest('dist', { sourcemaps: '.' })); // writes main.css.map next to main.css
```

[scss-compiler](/plugins/scss-compiler), [css-squeezer](/plugins/css-squeezer), [js-squeezer](/plugins/js-squeezer) and [file-concat](/plugins/file-concat) produce a map when the file has one, chained to the map before them where the tool supports it. Without `sourcemaps: true` they make none.

## Return `pipeline()`, not a `.pipe()` chain

When a stream in the middle of a `.pipe()` chain fails, gulp never hears the task end: it hangs at "Starting…" and a watcher stops running it. `pipeline` from `node:stream/promises` ends the task with the error:

```js
import { pipeline } from 'node:stream/promises';

export const styles = () => pipeline(src('src/scss/*.scss'), scssCompiler(), cssSqueezer(), dest('dist/css'));
```

In a dev task, start the watchers without returning them: a failing task is then reported and the next change runs it again, instead of the error ending the whole dev task.

```js
export const serve = (done) => {
  watch('src/scss/**', styles);
  done();
};
```

## ES modules and TypeScript gulpfiles

The packages are ES modules. Use them from:

* `gulpfile.mjs`, or `gulpfile.js` with `"type": "module"` in package.json: `import`.
* a CommonJS `gulpfile.js`: `const { cssSqueezer } = require('@zilero/gulp-css-squeezer')` (Node.js 22.12+ loads ES modules with `require`).
* `gulpfile.ts`. gulp-cli loads it through a register module it looks for in a fixed order: ts-node, sucrase, @babel/register, esbuild-register, @swc/register. Node's own TypeScript support is not registered for `require`, so without one of them gulp-cli prints an error for each before falling back. Install esbuild-register:

```sh
npm install --save-dev esbuild-register esbuild
```

It compiles the gulpfile and the files it imports on the fly, ES modules included (`"type": "module"`), on every supported Node.js. sucrase does not work with `"type": "module"`, and gulp-cli picks it before esbuild-register when it is installed. The compiled code runs as CommonJS, so top-level `await` is not available in the gulpfile.

The plugins ship their types, and `Vinyl` (the file type hooks receive) is exported by `@zilero/gulp-plugin-factory`.

## Files without contents and streams

`src(…, { read: false })` and directories give files without contents. The plugins pass them through untouched, except the ones that work on paths ([refilename](/plugins/refilename), [file-exclude](/plugins/file-exclude), [conditional](/plugins/conditional), [folder-clone](/plugins/folder-clone), [file-changed](/plugins/file-changed)).

`src(…, { buffer: false })` gives streamed contents. Only [archive-creator](/plugins/archive-creator) accepts them; the others emit `Streaming is not supported`.

# Recipes

## A complete site build

The [example project](/guide/example-project) is a static site built with every plugin: pages, styles, scripts, images and fonts, a dev server and a hashed, zipped release. Its page walks through each task.

## Incremental builds

* **In one watch session**, `src(globs, { since: lastRun(task) })` reads only the files changed since the task last ran. It suits tasks that copy files one to one.
* **Across runs** (restarting the dev server, running `gulp images` again), [file-changed](/plugins/file-changed) compares with what is already in the output folder. It suits slow work such as image and font encoding.
* Neither suits Sass, Pug or bundles, whose files depend on each other: rebuild their entry points.

## Responsive images

```js
src('src/images/photos/*.jpg', { encoding: false })
  .pipe(imageSqueezer({ formats: ['original', 'webp', 'avif'], widths: [480, 960, 1920] }))
  .pipe(dest('dist/images/photos'));
```

```html
<picture>
  <source type="image/avif" srcset="/images/photos/beach-480w.avif 480w, /images/photos/beach-960w.avif 960w" />
  <source type="image/webp" srcset="/images/photos/beach-480w.webp 480w, /images/photos/beach-960w.webp 960w" />
  <img src="/images/photos/beach-960w.jpg" srcset="/images/photos/beach-480w.jpg 480w" alt="" />
</picture>
```

## Only the glyphs a page needs

```js
src('src/fonts/Display.ttf', { encoding: false })
  .pipe(fontSwitcher({ formats: 'woff2', subset: 'ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789' }))
  .pipe(dest('dist/fonts'));
```

## A step in one mode only

Plugins are plain functions, so a JavaScript condition decides when the whole stream takes the same path:

```ts
import { PassThrough } from 'node:stream';

const when = ({ condition, then }) => (condition ? then() : new PassThrough({ objectMode: true }));
```

Use [conditional](/plugins/conditional) when the decision depends on each file.

url: /gulp-plugins-hub/guide/example-project.md

  A complete static site built with every gulp-plugins-hub plugin, set up the
  way a gulp 5 build is in 2026, with its task tree and how to run it.
---

# Example project

[`apps/example`](https://github.com/Zilero232/gulp-plugins-hub/tree/master/apps/example) is a static site built with every plugin: Pug pages, SCSS, an esbuild bundle and classic vendor scripts, responsive images, web fonts, hashed asset names and a zipped release. It is set up the way a gulp 5 build is in 2026: a TypeScript gulpfile loaded by esbuild-register, one task per file, `pipeline` everywhere and a browser-sync dev server.

CI builds it on every pull request from the packages' built `dist/` files, as a user would install them, and checks the output.

## Run it

From a clone of the repository:

```sh
bun install
bun run example             # builds the packages, then the site (gulp build --production)

cd apps/example
bunx gulp                   # build, serve with live reload, rebuild on change
bunx gulp build             # development build: readable output with source maps
bunx gulp build --production
bunx gulp release           # production build, hashed names in release/site/, release/site-v1.0.0.zip
bunx gulp --tasks           # the task tree below
```

`gulp release` always builds for production. `NODE_ENV=production` switches every task to production too, and `ANALYTICS_ID` fills in the measurement id of the analytics snippet.

## Layout

```text
apps/example/
├── gulpfile.ts          the public tasks: build, release, clean and the default dev task
├── .browserslistrc      the browsers css-squeezer prefixes and lowers syntax for
├── gulp/
│   ├── config.ts        paths, the production mode, the version from package.json
│   ├── tasks/           one task per file: pages, styles, scripts, assets, statics, revision, archive, serve, clean
│   └── utils/           the dev server, `when` for steps that run in one mode only, cleanup of deleted assets
├── src/
│   ├── pages/           Pug pages; templates/ has the layout they extend
│   ├── scss/            main.scss and its partials in config/, base/, components/, layout/
│   ├── js/              main.js and its modules (bundled), vendor/ (classic scripts)
│   ├── images/, fonts/  encoded and converted by the assets task
│   └── static/          copied as they are
└── test/                checks the output of `gulp release`
```

## Tasks

```text
├─┬ build    Build the site into dist/ (add --production for minified output)
│ └─┬ <series>
│   ├── clean
│   └─┬ <parallel>
│     ├── pages
│     ├── styles
│     ├─┬ <parallel>
│     │ ├── app
│     │ └── vendor
│     ├── assets
│     └── statics
├── clean    Remove dist/ and release/
├─┬ default  Build, serve with live reload and rebuild on change
│ └─┬ <series>
│   ├─┬ <parallel>  (pages, styles, scripts, assets, statics)
│   └── serve
└─┬ release  Build for production, hash the asset names into release/site/ and zip it
  └─┬ <series>
    ├── build
    ├── revision
    └── archive
```

| Task       | Plugins                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      | Output                                                              |
| ---------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `pages`    | [pug-compiler](/plugins/pug-compiler), [html-squeezer](/plugins/html-squeezer) in production                                                                                                                                                 | `dist/*.html`                                                       |
| `styles`   | [scss-compiler](/plugins/scss-compiler), [css-squeezer](/plugins/css-squeezer)                                                                                                                                                               | `dist/css/main.css`, a source map in development                    |
| `app`      | esbuild, called from the task                                                                                                                                                                                                                | `dist/js/app.js`                                                    |
| `vendor`   | [file-concat](/plugins/file-concat), [text-replace](/plugins/text-replace), [js-squeezer](/plugins/js-squeezer) in production                                                                                                                | `dist/js/vendor.js`                                                 |
| `assets`   | [file-exclude](/plugins/file-exclude), [file-changed](/plugins/file-changed), [conditional](/plugins/conditional), [image-squeezer](/plugins/image-squeezer), [font-switcher](/plugins/font-switcher), [folder-clone](/plugins/folder-clone) | WebP and AVIF images at two widths, woff2 and woff, `email/` copies |
| `statics`  | none: `src` and `dest` with `since: lastRun(statics)`                                                                                                                                                                                        | `robots.txt`, `favicon.svg`                                         |
| `revision` | [asset-revision](/plugins/asset-revision)                                                                                                                                                                                                    | `release/site/` with hashed names and `rev-manifest.json`           |
| `archive`  | [archive-creator](/plugins/archive-creator), [refilename](/plugins/refilename)                                                                                                                                                               | `release/site-v1.0.0.zip`                                           |

## The code

### Configuration

The mode is read once, when the gulpfile loads. gulp-cli has parsed the command line already, so `parseArgs` with `strict: false` only picks out the flag and the task names:

```ts
// gulp/config.ts
import { parseArgs } from 'node:util';

import packageJson from '../package.json' with { type: 'json' };

const { values, positionals } = parseArgs({
  options: { production: { type: 'boolean', default: false } },
  strict: false
});

export const production =
  values.production === true || process.env.NODE_ENV === 'production' || positionals.includes('release');

export const { version } = packageJson;
```

### Pages

```ts
export const pages = (): Promise<void> =>
  pipeline(
    gulp.src('src/pages/**/*.pug'),
    pugCompiler({
      pugOptions: { basedir: 'src', pretty: !production }, // `extends /templates/_layout.pug` resolves from src/
      data: ({ file }) => ({ page: file.stem, year: new Date().getFullYear(), version, production })
    }),
    when({ condition: production, then: () => htmlSqueezer({ preset: 'comprehensive' }) }),
    gulp.dest('dist')
  );
```

### Styles, with source maps in development

```ts
export const styles = (): Promise<void> =>
  pipeline(
    gulp.src('src/scss/*.scss', { sourcemaps: !production }), // the entry files; partials come in through @use
    scssCompiler(),
    cssSqueezer({ minify: production }), // prefixes and lowers syntax for .browserslistrc
    gulp.dest('dist/css', { sourcemaps: '.' }),
    // While the dev server runs, browser-sync injects the new CSS without a reload.
    when({ condition: server.active, then: () => server.stream({ match: '**/*.css' }) })
  );
```

### Scripts

The application's modules go through a bundler, called from the task; gulp plugins handle what bundlers do not:

```ts
const app = async (): Promise<void> => {
  await build({ entryPoints: ['src/js/main.js'], outfile: 'dist/js/app.js', bundle: true, minify: production });
};

// Third-party snippets that stay classic scripts: joined in order, filled in, minified in production.
const vendor = (): Promise<void> =>
  pipeline(
    gulp.src('src/js/vendor/*.js', { sourcemaps: !production }),
    fileConcat({ name: 'vendor.js', order: 'polyfills.js' }),
    textReplace({
      rules: [
        { search: '__ANALYTICS_ID__', replace: process.env.ANALYTICS_ID ?? 'G-EXAMPLE' },
        { search: '__VERSION__', replace: version }
      ]
    }),
    when({ condition: production, then: () => jsSqueezer() }),
    gulp.dest('dist/js', { sourcemaps: '.' })
  );

export const scripts = gulp.parallel(app, vendor);
```

### Images and fonts in one task

Encoding is the slow part, so everything that can drop a file runs first: file-exclude, then file-changed, which skips the files whose output in `dist/` is newer, across restarts of the dev server too.

```ts
export const assets = (): Promise<void> =>
  pipeline(
    gulp.src('src/{images,fonts}/**', { encoding: false }),
    fileExclude({ patterns: ['*.psd', '.DS_Store'], size: { max: 2 * 1024 * 1024 } }),
    fileChanged({ dest: 'dist', target: builtPath }), // builtPath: one of the files written for the source
    conditional({
      handlers: [
        {
          condition: ({ file }) => isHero(file),
          handler: () => imageSqueezer({ formats: heroFormats, widths: [640, 1280] })
        },
        { condition: ({ file }) => isImage(file), handler: () => imageSqueezer({ formats: ['original', 'webp'] }) },
        { condition: ({ file }) => isFont(file), handler: () => fontSwitcher({ formats: ['woff2', 'woff'] }) }
      ]
    }),
    // Email clients do not show WebP or AVIF: email/ gets a copy of the JPEG and PNG images only.
    folderClone({
      dirs: 'email',
      onClone: ({ file, original }) => (isImage(file) && original.relative.startsWith('images') ? file : null)
    }),
    gulp.dest('dist')
  );
```

### Release: hashed names and a zip

```ts
const revision = (): Promise<void> =>
  pipeline(
    gulp.src('dist/**', { encoding: false }),
    assetRevision({ exclude: ['*.html', '*.map', 'robots.txt'], manifest: true }), // robots.txt keeps its name
    gulp.dest('release/site')
  );

const archive = (): Promise<void> =>
  pipeline(
    gulp.src('release/site/**', { encoding: false }),
    archiveCreator({ name: 'site.zip' }),
    refilename({ suffix: `-v${version}` }),
    gulp.dest('release')
  );

export const release = gulp.series(build, revision, archive);
```

### Dev server

The watchers are not returned: a failing task is reported, and the next change runs it again. A deleted source is removed from `dist/` too: a static file directly, an image or font with every format and width built from it.

```ts
export const serve: TaskFunction = (done) => {
  server.init({ server: 'dist', open: false, notify: false, ui: false });

  gulp.watch('src/**/*.pug', gulp.series(pages, reload));
  gulp.watch('src/scss/**', styles);
  gulp.watch('src/js/**', gulp.series(scripts, reload));
  gulp.watch('src/{images,fonts}/**', gulp.series(assets, reload)).on('unlink', removeBuilt);
  gulp.watch('src/static/**', gulp.series(statics, reload)).on('unlink', (file) => rm(toDist(file), { force: true }));

  done();
};
```

## What the test checks

`bun run test` in `apps/example` runs `gulp release`, then [`test/release.test.ts`](https://github.com/Zilero232/gulp-plugins-hub/blob/master/apps/example/test/release.test.ts): minified pages with their data, prefixed CSS without source maps, the esbuild bundle, the vendor scripts in order, woff2 fonts that keep their OpenType tables, WebP and AVIF images at both widths, the `email/` copies, the hashed names with every reference rewritten, and the zip.

---

---
url: /gulp-plugins-hub/guide/writing-plugins.md
description: >-
  Build a typed gulp plugin with @zilero/gulp-plugin-factory: a stream from a
  transform function, validated options, source maps, hooks and tests.
---

# Writing a plugin

Every plugin in the hub is built with `@zilero/gulp-plugin-factory`. It turns a function that changes one file into a stream that follows the [gulp plugin guidelines](https://github.com/gulpjs/gulp/blob/master/docs/writing-a-plugin/guidelines.md): files without contents pass through, streamed contents are refused, errors become `PluginError`s with the plugin name and file and are emitted rather than thrown, and files leave in the order they came.

```sh
npm install @zilero/gulp-plugin-factory zod
```

## A banner plugin

```ts
import { createPlugin, parseOptions } from '@zilero/gulp-plugin-factory';
import { z } from 'zod';

const PLUGIN_NAME = 'gulp-banner';

const optionsSchema = z
  .object({ text: z.string().min(1), extensions: z.array(z.string()).default(['.js', '.css']) })
  .strict();

export type BannerOptions = z.input<typeof optionsSchema>;

export const banner = (options: BannerOptions) => {
  // Checked when the plugin is created: invalid options throw a PluginError listing every problem.
  const { text, extensions } = parseOptions({ name: PLUGIN_NAME, schema: optionsSchema, options });

  return createPlugin({
    name: PLUGIN_NAME,
    // Other files pass through untouched; extensions are compared in lowercase.
    extensions,
    transform: (file) => {
      file.contents = Buffer.concat([Buffer.from(`${text}\n`), file.contents]);
    }
  });
};
```

## What `transform` returns

| Return            | Effect                                                   |
| ----------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| nothing           | The file, changed in place, goes on.                     |
| `null`            | The file is dropped.                                     |
| a file            | That file goes on instead.                               |
| an array of files | Each of them goes on, in order: one input, many outputs. |

`transform` may be async; the next file waits for it. To emit files that do not come from one input (a bundle, a manifest), collect in `transform`, return `null`, and `push` the result from `flush`:

```ts
import { createPlugin, Vinyl } from '@zilero/gulp-plugin-factory';
import path from 'node:path';

export const fileList = () => {
  const names: string[] = [];

  return createPlugin({
    name: 'gulp-file-list',
    transform: (file) => {
      names.push(file.relative);
      return null;
    },
    // A path under the working directory, so `dest('dist')` writes dist/files.txt.
    flush: ({ push }) => push(new Vinyl({ path: path.resolve('files.txt'), contents: Buffer.from(names.join('\n')) }))
  });
};
```

## Files without contents and streams

By default `transform` gets only files with Buffer contents (`accept: 'buffer'`): files without contents pass through and streamed contents emit `Streaming is not supported`. Set `accept: 'any'` to get every file, for plugins that work on paths or handle streams themselves.

## Choosing the files

`extensions: ['.css', '.scss']` limits `transform` to those extensions (compared in lowercase, so `MAIN.CSS` counts); other files pass through untouched. `filter` takes any other test and is checked together with `extensions`. For user-facing include or exclude lists, `createPathMatcher` turns globs and regular expressions into one test of the path relative to the base: a glob without `/` (`*.min.js`) matches the file name in any folder, a glob with `/` (`vendor/**`) matches from the base, and a RegExp tests the path with `/` separators.

```ts
import { createPathMatcher, createPlugin } from '@zilero/gulp-plugin-factory';

const isExcluded = createPathMatcher({ patterns: ['*.min.js', 'vendor/**', /\.generated\./] });

createPlugin({
  name: 'gulp-my-minifier',
  extensions: ['.js', '.mjs'],
  filter: (file) => !isExcluded(file.relative),
  transform: (file) => {
    // only .js and .mjs files that are not excluded get here
  }
});
```

## Cleaning up

A plugin that starts something long-lived (a compiler process, a worker pool) closes it in `dispose`. It runs once whichever way the stream is done: after the last file, on an error, or when the stream is destroyed, where `flush` never runs.

```ts
let compiler: Compiler | undefined;

createPlugin({
  name: 'gulp-my-compiler',
  transform: async (file) => {
    compiler ??= await startCompiler();
    file.contents = Buffer.from(await compiler.compile(file.contents.toString()));
  },
  dispose: () => compiler?.close()
});
```

## Source maps

When `src(…, { sourcemaps: true })` gave the file a map, pass it to the tool as its input map and store the tool's map:

```ts
import { applySourceMap, createPlugin, getInputSourceMap, toPosixPath } from '@zilero/gulp-plugin-factory';

createPlugin({
  name: 'gulp-my-minifier',
  transform: async (file) => {
    const result = await minify(file.contents.toString(), {
      filename: toPosixPath(file.relative), // `/` on every OS, or Windows maps get backslashes
      sourceMap: Boolean(file.sourceMap),
      inputSourceMap: getInputSourceMap(file) // undefined when there is nothing to chain
    });

    file.contents = Buffer.from(result.code);
    if (file.sourceMap && result.map) applySourceMap({ file, map: result.map });
  }
});
```

For a tool that cannot take an input map, let `applySourceMap` chain it: `applySourceMap({ file, map, chain: true })`. Only the sources that are the file itself get its map; other sources of the tool's map (an inlined import) stay as they are. To chain several inputs into one map yourself (a bundle), `getChainableSourceMap(file)` gives each file's map with absolute `file://` sources, ready for `@jridgewell/remapping`. Sources that are already URLs (`webpack://…`, `data:…`) are kept; `isUrl(value)` makes the same check.

A plugin that renames or moves a file calls `syncSourceMapFile(file)` afterwards, so `dest(…, { sourcemaps: '.' })` writes the map for the new name:

```ts
transform: (file) => {
  file.stem += '.min';
  syncSourceMapFile(file); // file.sourceMap.file is now 'js/app.min.js'; files without a map are left alone
};
```

## Binary files

Set `binary: true` in plugins for images, fonts or other binary formats. When gulp 5 read the file as UTF-8 (no `src(globs, { encoding: false })`), the file emits an error that tells the user how to fix it, instead of reaching `transform` corrupted. The check is `assertBinaryContents(file)`, exported for plugins that need it elsewhere.

```ts
createPlugin({
  name: 'gulp-my-images',
  extensions: ['.png', '.jpg'],
  binary: true,
  transform: async (file) => {
    file.contents = await optimize(file.contents);
  }
});
```

## Options with any schema library

`parseOptions` takes any synchronous [Standard Schema](https://standardschema.dev): zod 4, valibot, arktype and others. Check callbacks with `isFunction` rather than zod's `z.function()`, which wraps the function and validates its result, and breaks async hooks. `ContentHook` is the type of a hook on a file's text, `FileHookInput` (`{ file }`) the input of a hook on a file, and `isRelativePathInside` checks paths that must stay inside an output folder:

```ts
import type { ContentHook } from '@zilero/gulp-plugin-factory';

import { isFunction, isRelativePathInside } from '@zilero/gulp-plugin-factory';
import { z } from 'zod';

const optionsSchema = z
  .object({
    name: z.string().refine(isRelativePathInside, 'Expected a path inside the output folder'),
    onBeforeWrite: z.custom<ContentHook>(isFunction, 'Expected a function').optional()
  })
  .strict();
```

## Hooks

Hooks take one object and may return a promise. Run a hook on a file's text with `runContentHook`: without a hook it returns the text as it is, and a hook written in JavaScript that forgets to return the text gets a clear error (`onBeforeWrite must return the text as a string, got undefined`) instead of an obscure one from `Buffer.from`.

```ts
import { runContentHook } from '@zilero/gulp-plugin-factory';

transform: async (file) => {
  const content = await runContentHook({
    name: 'onBeforeWrite',
    hook: onBeforeWrite,
    content: file.contents.toString(),
    file
  });

  file.contents = Buffer.from(content);
};
```

For other hooks, type the input with `FileHookInput` and add what the hook needs: `type CloneInput = FileHookInput & { dir: string }`.

## Testing

```ts
import { createFile, getContents, runPlugin } from '@zilero/gulp-plugin-factory/testing';
import { expect, it } from 'vitest';

import { banner } from './banner';

it('adds the banner to scripts only', async () => {
  const [script, image] = await runPlugin(banner({ text: '/*! hi */' }), [
    createFile({ path: 'app.js', contents: 'run();' }),
    createFile({ path: 'logo.png', contents: 'png' })
  ]);

  expect(getContents(script).toString()).toBe('/*! hi */\nrun();');
  expect(getContents(image).toString()).toBe('png');
});
```

Compare paths with `getRelativePath(file)`, which uses `/` on every OS, so the tests pass on Windows too.

The full API is in the [factory reference](/reference/factory) and the [testing reference](/reference/testing).

---

---
url: /gulp-plugins-hub/guide/troubleshooting.md
description: >-
  Fixes for the problems gulp 5 builds run into with gulp-plugins-hub -
  corrupted binary files, CommonJS and TypeScript gulpfiles, native binaries in
  CI and Windows paths.
---

# Troubleshooting

## Images, fonts or archives come out corrupted

Gulp 5 reads every file as UTF-8 text unless told otherwise, and every byte that is not valid UTF-8 becomes `U+FFFD`. [image-squeezer](/plugins/image-squeezer) and [font-switcher](/plugins/font-switcher) notice and fail with the fix:

```text
Error in plugin "@zilero/gulp-image-squeezer"
Message:
    images/hero.jpg was read as UTF-8 text and is corrupted. Read binary files with `src(globs, { encoding: false })`
```

Read binary files with `encoding: false`:

```js
src('src/images/**', { encoding: false });
```

Plugins that only copy, rename or pack files ([archive-creator](/plugins/archive-creator), [asset-revision](/plugins/asset-revision), [folder-clone](/plugins/folder-clone), [refilename](/plugins/refilename)) cannot tell a corrupted file from a good one: give them `encoding: false` too whenever the stream has binary files. Text plugins work with either; [text-replace](/plugins/text-replace) leaves files with a NUL byte alone.

## `require()` of the plugins in a CommonJS gulpfile

The packages are ES modules. Node.js 22.12 and newer load them with `require`, through the named export:

```js
// gulpfile.js (CommonJS)
const { scssCompiler } = require('@zilero/gulp-scss-compiler');
```

* `scssCompiler is not a function`: `require` returns the module namespace, so the default export is `require(…).default`. Use the named export.
* `ERR_REQUIRE_ESM`: the Node.js version is older than 22.12. The packages need 22.13 or newer.
* On some 22.x releases Node.js prints an `ExperimentalWarning` for `require()` of an ES module. It is harmless; moving the gulpfile to ES modules (`gulpfile.mjs`, or `"type": "module"`) removes it.

## A TypeScript gulpfile does not load

gulp-cli loads `gulpfile.ts` through a register module, tried in a fixed order: ts-node, sucrase, @babel/register, esbuild-register, @swc/register. Node's built-in type stripping is not registered for `require`, which gulp-cli uses, so it does not help here.

* `Failed to load external module …` for each of them: none is installed. Install `esbuild-register` and `esbuild`.
* The gulpfile fails to load with `"type": "module"` although esbuild-register is installed, and the log says `Loaded external module: sucrase/register/ts`: sucrase is picked before esbuild-register, and it does not handle ES modules. `npm ls sucrase` shows what brings it in; remove it.
* `Top-level await is currently not supported with the "cjs" output format`: the register modules compile the gulpfile to CommonJS. Move the `await` into a task.

[Gulp 5 essentials](/guide/gulp-5#es-modules-and-typescript-gulpfiles) has the setup; the [example project](/guide/example-project) uses it.

## Native binaries missing in CI or Docker

[image-squeezer](/plugins/image-squeezer) (sharp), [scss-compiler](/plugins/scss-compiler) (sass-embedded) and [css-squeezer](/plugins/css-squeezer) (Lightning CSS) ship a prebuilt binary per platform as an optional dependency, such as `@img/sharp-linux-x64`, `sass-embedded-linux-x64` or `lightningcss-linux-x64-gnu`. The package manager installs only the one for the machine it runs on. Errors like `Could not load the "sharp" module using the linux-x64 runtime` or `Cannot find module 'lightningcss-linux-x64-gnu'` mean that binary is missing:

* Install on the machine (or in the image) that runs the build. A `node_modules` copied from macOS or Windows into a Linux container has the wrong binaries.
* Do not skip optional dependencies: no `--omit=optional`, `--no-optional` or `optional=false` in `.npmrc`.
* Alpine and other musl images need the `musl` builds; they install when `npm install` runs inside that image.
* With npm, a lockfile written on one platform can miss the optional packages of another. Run `npm install` once more on the CI platform, or install them explicitly: `npm install --os=linux --cpu=x64 sharp`. Bun and pnpm keep every platform in the lockfile.

font-switcher uses WebAssembly, so it has no native binary.

## Paths on Windows

`file.relative` and `file.path` use the platform's separator, so on Windows they contain `\`. Globs and regular expressions in plugin options are matched against the path with `/` on every platform: write `'images/**/*.png'` or `/^images\//` and they work everywhere.

In your own hooks and conditions, compare paths the same way:

```js
import path from 'node:path';

const relative = file.relative.split(path.sep).join('/');
```

Names the plugins write into files (archive entries, the asset-revision manifest, source map sources, error messages) always use `/`.

## A task hangs at "Starting…"

A stream in the middle of a `.pipe()` chain failed, and gulp never heard the task end. Return `pipeline(…)` from `node:stream/promises` instead: the task then ends with the error ([why](/guide/gulp-5#return-pipeline-not-a-pipe-chain)).

## `Invalid options` before any file is read

Every plugin validates its options when it is created and lists every problem:

```text
Error in plugin "@zilero/gulp-css-squeezer"
Message:
    Invalid options:
    • Unrecognized key: "minfy"
```

Unknown keys are errors, so a typo or an option name from another plugin shows up here instead of being ignored. The plugin's page lists its options, and [Migrating from other plugins](/guide/migrating-from-other-plugins) maps the common ones.

---

---
url: /gulp-plugins-hub/guide/migrating-from-other-plugins.md
description: >-
  Replace gulp-sass, gulp-clean-css, gulp-autoprefixer, gulp-terser,
  gulp-htmlmin, gulp-imagemin, gulp-rev, gulp-zip, gulp-if, gulp-rename,
  gulp-concat and others with typed gulp 5 plugins, option by option.
---

# Migrating from other plugins

Each plugin here replaces one or more of the plugins a gulp build usually has. The options differ, but the job is the same; this page maps the common cases. Every plugin page ends with a full migration table.

Two things change everywhere:

* **Errors end the task.** No `.on('error', sass.logError)` or `plumber()`: return `pipeline(…)` and an error ends the task with the file and line, while a watcher keeps watching ([why](/guide/gulp-5#return-pipeline-not-a-pipe-chain)).
* **Options are checked when the plugin is created.** An option name carried over from the old plugin fails with `Unrecognized key` instead of being ignored.

## At a glance

| You use                                                                                     | Use instead                                                                | Notes                                                                    |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| gulp-sass, gulp-dart-sass                                                                   | [scss-compiler](/plugins/scss-compiler)                                    | sass-embedded, one compiler per stream; `sassOptions` are Sass's options |
| gulp-clean-css, gulp-cssnano, gulp-autoprefixer, gulp-postcss with autoprefixer and cssnano | [css-squeezer](/plugins/css-squeezer)                                      | Lightning CSS: minify, prefix and lower syntax in one pass               |
| gulp-terser, gulp-uglify                                                                    | [js-squeezer](/plugins/js-squeezer)                                        | terser; `terserOptions`                                                  |
| gulp-htmlmin                                                                                | [html-squeezer](/plugins/html-squeezer)                                    | html-minifier-next, the same option names; a preset by default           |
| gulp-pug                                                                                    | [pug-compiler](/plugins/pug-compiler)                                      | `pugOptions` and `data`                                                  |
| gulp-imagemin, gulp-webp, gulp-avif, gulp-responsive                                        | [image-squeezer](/plugins/image-squeezer)                                  | sharp; formats and widths in one plugin                                  |
| gulp-ttf2woff2, gulp-ttf2woff, gulp-fonter                                                  | [font-switcher](/plugins/font-switcher)                                    | several formats at once, subsetting                                      |
| gulp-rev with gulp-rev-rewrite                                                              | [asset-revision](/plugins/asset-revision)                                  | hashes, rewritten references and the manifest in one pass                |
| gulp-zip, gulp-tar                                                                          | [archive-creator](/plugins/archive-creator)                                | zip, tar and tar.gz                                                      |
| gulp-concat                                                                                 | [file-concat](/plugins/file-concat)                                        | an explicit order, a header and footer                                   |
| gulp-replace, gulp-header, gulp-footer                                                      | [text-replace](/plugins/text-replace)                                      | rules, async replacers, a header and footer                              |
| gulp-rename                                                                                 | [refilename](/plugins/refilename)                                          | `stem` instead of `basename`                                             |
| gulp-if                                                                                     | [conditional](/plugins/conditional)                                        | checked per file, else-if branches                                       |
| gulp-filter                                                                                 | [file-exclude](/plugins/file-exclude), [conditional](/plugins/conditional) | drop files, or send some through other plugins                           |
| gulp-newer, gulp-changed                                                                    | [file-changed](/plugins/file-changed)                                      | by modification time or contents                                         |

## Sass: gulp-sass

```js
// Before
import gulpSass from 'gulp-sass';
import * as dartSass from 'sass';
const sass = gulpSass(dartSass);

src('src/scss/*.scss')
  .pipe(sass({ outputStyle: 'compressed', includePaths: ['node_modules'] }).on('error', sass.logError))
  .pipe(dest('dist/css'));

// After
import scssCompiler from '@zilero/gulp-scss-compiler';

pipeline(
  src('src/scss/*.scss'),
  scssCompiler({ sassOptions: { style: 'compressed', loadPaths: ['node_modules'] } }),
  dest('dist/css')
);
```

`sassOptions` takes the options of Sass's modern API: `style` instead of `outputStyle`, `loadPaths` instead of `includePaths`. Partials (`_*.scss`) are skipped, and source maps follow `src(…, { sourcemaps: true })`.

## CSS: gulp-clean-css and gulp-autoprefixer

```js
// Before
src('dist/css/*.css')
  .pipe(autoprefixer())
  .pipe(cleanCSS({ level: 2 }))
  .pipe(dest('dist/css'));

// After
import cssSqueezer from '@zilero/gulp-css-squeezer';

pipeline(src('dist/css/*.css'), cssSqueezer(), dest('dist/css'));
```

css-squeezer reads the browsers from `.browserslistrc` (or the `browserslist` key of package.json) like autoprefixer, or from `targets: 'defaults'`. `minify: false` only prefixes and lowers syntax.

## JavaScript: gulp-terser and gulp-uglify

```js
// Before
src('src/js/*.js')
  .pipe(terser({ compress: { drop_console: true }, format: { comments: false } }))
  .pipe(dest('dist/js'));

// After
import jsSqueezer from '@zilero/gulp-js-squeezer';

pipeline(
  src('src/js/*.js'),
  jsSqueezer({ terserOptions: { compress: { drop_console: true }, format: { comments: false } } }),
  dest('dist/js')
);
```

gulp-uglify's `output` is terser's `format`. Source maps are chained to the input's when the file has one.

## HTML: gulp-htmlmin

```js
// Before
src('dist/*.html')
  .pipe(htmlmin({ collapseWhitespace: true, removeComments: true }))
  .pipe(dest('dist'));

// After
import htmlSqueezer from '@zilero/gulp-html-squeezer';

pipeline(
  src('dist/*.html'),
  htmlSqueezer({ preset: false, htmlMinifierOptions: { collapseWhitespace: true, removeComments: true } }),
  dest('dist')
);
```

html-minifier-next keeps html-minifier's option names. Without `preset: false` the `conservative` preset applies, with your options on top; `preset: 'comprehensive'` also minifies inline CSS, JavaScript and SVG.

## Pug: gulp-pug

```js
// Before
src('src/pages/*.pug')
  .pipe(pug({ pretty: true, data: { year: 2026 } }))
  .pipe(dest('dist'));

// After
import pugCompiler from '@zilero/gulp-pug-compiler';

pipeline(
  src('src/pages/*.pug'),
  pugCompiler({ pugOptions: { pretty: true }, data: ({ file }) => ({ page: file.stem, year: 2026 }) }),
  dest('dist')
);
```

`data` is an object or a function of the file. Files whose name starts with `_` are skipped (`skipPartials`).

## Images: gulp-imagemin, gulp-webp, gulp-responsive

```js
// Before
src('src/images/*')
  .pipe(imagemin([mozjpeg({ quality: 75 }), optipng()]))
  .pipe(dest('dist/images'));
src('src/images/*.jpg').pipe(webp()).pipe(dest('dist/images'));

// After
import imageSqueezer from '@zilero/gulp-image-squeezer';

pipeline(
  src('src/images/*', { encoding: false }),
  imageSqueezer({ formats: ['original', 'webp'], quality: 75, widths: [640, 1280] }),
  dest('dist/images')
);
```

One plugin re-encodes, converts (`webp`, `avif`, `jpeg`, `png`) and resizes (`hero-640w.jpg`, …). SVG and other files it does not read pass through. Read images with `encoding: false`.

## Fonts: gulp-ttf2woff2

```js
// Before
src('src/fonts/*.ttf').pipe(ttf2woff2()).pipe(dest('dist/fonts'));

// After
import fontSwitcher from '@zilero/gulp-font-switcher';

pipeline(
  src('src/fonts/*.{ttf,otf}', { encoding: false }),
  fontSwitcher({ formats: ['woff2', 'woff'] }),
  dest('dist/fonts')
);
```

`subset: 'ABC…'` keeps only the glyphs you use; `keepOriginal: true` emits the source font too.

## Cache-busting: gulp-rev and gulp-rev-rewrite

```js
// Before: two passes and a manifest file between them
src('dist/**/*.{css,js,png,woff2}').pipe(rev()).pipe(dest('dist')).pipe(rev.manifest()).pipe(dest('dist'));
src('dist/**/*.html')
  .pipe(revRewrite({ manifest: readFileSync('dist/rev-manifest.json') }))
  .pipe(dest('dist'));

// After
import assetRevision from '@zilero/gulp-asset-revision';

pipeline(src('dist/**', { encoding: false }), assetRevision({ manifest: true }), dest('release'));
```

One pass hashes the file names, except pages, source maps and the files fetched at fixed URLs such as `robots.txt` and the favicon (`exclude` lists them), rewrites the references in HTML, CSS, JavaScript, SVG, JSON and the other text files, and writes `rev-manifest.json` when `manifest` is set.

## Archives: gulp-zip

```js
// Before
src('dist/**').pipe(zip('site.zip')).pipe(dest('release'));

// After
import archiveCreator from '@zilero/gulp-archive-creator';

pipeline(src('dist/**', { encoding: false }), archiveCreator({ name: 'site.zip' }), dest('release'));
```

The extension of `name` picks the format: `.zip`, `.tar`, `.tgz` or `.tar.gz`.

## Joining files: gulp-concat

```js
// Before
src(['src/js/polyfills.js', 'src/js/*.js'])
  .pipe(concat('vendor.js', { newLine: ';\n' }))
  .pipe(dest('dist/js'));

// After
import fileConcat from '@zilero/gulp-file-concat';

pipeline(
  src('src/js/*.js'),
  fileConcat({ name: 'vendor.js', order: 'polyfills.js', separator: ';\n' }),
  dest('dist/js')
);
```

Gulp 5 does not keep the order of the globs given to `src`, so the order goes in `order`.

## Replacing text: gulp-replace

```js
// Before
src('dist/js/*.js')
  .pipe(replace('__VERSION__', version))
  .pipe(replace(/console\.log\(.*?\);?/g, ''))
  .pipe(dest('dist/js'));

// After
import textReplace from '@zilero/gulp-text-replace';

pipeline(
  src('dist/js/*.js'),
  textReplace({
    rules: [
      { search: '__VERSION__', replace: version },
      { search: /console\.log\(.*?\);?/g, replace: '' }
    ]
  }),
  dest('dist/js')
);
```

A string matches everywhere it occurs, as in gulp-replace. A replacer function gets one object, `({ match, groups, namedGroups, file })`, and may be async. `header` and `footer` replace gulp-header and gulp-footer.

## Renaming: gulp-rename

```js
// Before
src('dist/js/app.js')
  .pipe(rename({ basename: 'bundle', suffix: '.min' }))
  .pipe(dest('dist/js'));
src('dist/js/*.js')
  .pipe(
    rename((path) => {
      path.dirname = 'scripts';
    })
  )
  .pipe(dest('dist'));

// After
import refilename from '@zilero/gulp-refilename';

pipeline(src('dist/js/app.js'), refilename({ stem: 'bundle', suffix: '.min' }), dest('dist/js'));
pipeline(
  src('dist/js/*.js'),
  refilename(({ parts }) => {
    parts.dirname = 'scripts';
  }),
  dest('dist')
);
```

`basename` is `stem`; `prefix`, `suffix`, `extname` and `dirname` keep their names. A function gets `{ parts, file }` and changes `parts` or returns the changes; a string is the new file name.

## Conditions: gulp-if

```js
// Before
src('src/js/*.js').pipe(gulpif(production, terser())).pipe(dest('dist/js'));
src('src/**')
  .pipe(gulpif('*.css', cleanCSS(), gulpif('*.js', terser())))
  .pipe(dest('dist'));

// After
import conditional from '@zilero/gulp-conditional';

pipeline(
  src('src/**'),
  conditional({
    handlers: [
      { condition: '*.css', handler: () => cssSqueezer() },
      { condition: ({ file }) => file.extname === '.js', handler: () => jsSqueezer() }
    ]
  }),
  dest('dist')
);
```

The condition is checked for every file: a boolean, a glob or RegExp against `file.relative`, or a function of the file. The first branch that matches gets the file, the others pass through untouched (or go to `defaultHandler`, the else branch); a handler is created on first use and may return several plugins in an array. For a single condition that is the same for every file, a plain `production ? jsSqueezer() : new PassThrough({ objectMode: true })` is enough ([recipe](/guide/recipes#a-step-in-one-mode-only)).

## Filtering: gulp-filter

```js
// Before
src('dist/**')
  .pipe(filter(['**', '!**/*.map']))
  .pipe(dest('release'));

// After
import fileExclude from '@zilero/gulp-file-exclude';

pipeline(src('dist/**', { encoding: false }), fileExclude({ patterns: '*.map' }), dest('release'));
```

A glob without a slash matches the file name in any folder. file-exclude also drops by `size: { min, max }` or your own `exclude` function. gulp-filter's `restore` (send some files through a plugin, keep the rest) is [conditional](/plugins/conditional) with a glob condition.

## Changed files: gulp-newer and gulp-changed

```js
// Before
src('src/images/*.jpg').pipe(newer('dist/images')).pipe(imagemin()).pipe(dest('dist/images'));
src('src/static/**')
  .pipe(changed('dist', { hasChanged: changed.compareContents }))
  .pipe(dest('dist'));

// After
import fileChanged from '@zilero/gulp-file-changed';

pipeline(
  src('src/images/*.jpg', { encoding: false }),
  fileChanged({ dest: 'dist/images' }),
  imageSqueezer(),
  dest('dist/images')
);
pipeline(src('src/static/**', { encoding: false }), fileChanged({ dest: 'dist', compare: 'contents' }), dest('dist'));
```

`compare: 'contents'` is gulp-changed's `compareContents`. `extname` replaces `extension` (gulp-changed) and `ext` (gulp-newer), for builds that change the extension; `target` maps a source to its built path when the build renames it in other ways (gulp-newer's `map`).

---

---
url: /gulp-plugins-hub/guide/migration.md
description: >-
  Upgrade gulp-plugins-hub packages from 1.x to 2.0, with before and after code
  for hooks, the plugin factory, file-exclude, archive-creator, scss-compiler
  and the minifiers.
---

# Migrating from 1.x

2.0 rewrites every package for gulp 5 and Node.js 22.13+. The packages keep their names; the options changed where 1.x had bugs or nested everything under `pluginOptions`.

## Everywhere

* **Node.js 22.13+**, ES modules. In a CommonJS gulpfile use the named export: `const { scssCompiler } = require('@zilero/gulp-scss-compiler')`.
* **gulp is no longer a peer dependency**, as the [gulp guidelines](https://github.com/gulpjs/gulp/blob/master/docs/writing-a-plugin/guidelines.md) ask.
* **Hooks are flat and get the file**: `pluginOptions: { onBeforeMinify(content) }` became `onBeforeMinify({ content, file })`.
* **Errors** are `PluginError`s with the plugin name and file, emitted on the stream. Invalid options list every problem instead of printing a box and throwing an empty error.
* **Files without contents** (directories, `read: false`) pass through instead of failing with `File is null`.
* **Files outside a plugin's formats pass through**: the minifiers and compilers only touch their own extensions.
* **Binary files** need `src(globs, { encoding: false })` with gulp 5; image and font plugins say so when they get a file read as text.

## Package by package

| Package              | 1.x                                                                                            | 2.0                                                                                                                                                |
| -------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| gulp-plugin-factory  | `GulpPluginFactory({ pluginName, onFile, onFinish })`; `undefined` dropped the file            | `createPlugin({ name, transform, flush })`; nothing returned keeps the file, `null` drops it. Plus `parseOptions`, source map and testing helpers. |
| gulp-refilename      | object only                                                                                    | also a file name string or a function of the path parts                                                                                            |
| gulp-file-exclude    | `patterns` matched as substrings; `size: [min, max]`; `onExclude`                              | `patterns` are globs or RegExps; `size: { min, max }`; `exclude`                                                                                   |
| gulp-conditional     | the condition was checked once, for the whole stream                                           | checked per file, conditions get the file, branches created on first use                                                                           |
| gulp-folder-clone    | `onBeforeCopy`; files passed through unchanged                                                 | copies every file into `dirs`; `keepOriginal`, `onClone`                                                                                           |
| gulp-archive-creator | `format`, `archiveOptions`, `pluginOptions.archiveName`                                        | `name` (format from its extension), `format`, `archiverOptions`, `emptyArchive`, `directories`; tgz                                                |
| gulp-font-switcher   | fontmin; `pluginOptions.format`, `fontOptions.glyph`                                           | harfbuzz subsetting and fontverter, every OpenType table kept (no native build); `formats` (several at once), `subset`, `hinting`, `keepOriginal`  |
| gulp-html-squeezer   | html-minifier-terser, nothing minified without options                                         | html-minifier-next, `preset: 'conservative'` by default                                                                                            |
| gulp-js-squeezer     | `minifyOptions`, no source maps                                                                | `terserOptions`, source maps chained                                                                                                               |
| gulp-pug-compiler    | rendered the file on disk, partials included                                                   | renders the contents; `data`, `extname`, `skipPartials`                                                                                            |
| gulp-scss-compiler   | `scssOptions`; compiled the file on disk (`onBeforeCompile` was ignored), one process per file | `sassOptions`; compiles the contents with one compiler per stream; partials skipped; source maps; `.sass`                                          |

Each plugin page ends with its own migration notes.

## Before and after

### Hooks

```js
// 1.x
jsSqueezer({ pluginOptions: { onBeforeMinify: (content) => content.replace('__DEV__', 'false') } });

// 2.0: flat, one object with the file, may be async
jsSqueezer({ onBeforeMinify: ({ content, file }) => content.replace('__DEV__', 'false') });
```

### A plugin of your own

```js
// 1.x
GulpPluginFactory({
  pluginName: 'gulp-banner',
  onFile: (file) => {
    /* returning undefined dropped the file */
  }
});

// 2.0: nothing returned keeps the file, null drops it
import { createPlugin } from '@zilero/gulp-plugin-factory';

export const banner = () =>
  createPlugin({
    name: 'gulp-banner',
    transform: (file) => {
      file.contents = Buffer.concat([Buffer.from('/* banner */\n'), file.contents]);
    }
  });
```

[Writing a plugin](/guide/writing-plugins) covers options, source maps and tests.

### file-exclude

```js
// 1.x: substrings, a size tuple, onExclude
fileExclude({ patterns: ['.map', 'draft'], size: [0, 2_000_000], onExclude: (file) => file.stem === 'tmp' });

// 2.0: globs or RegExps, a size object, exclude
fileExclude({
  patterns: ['*.map', '**/draft/**'],
  size: { max: 2_000_000 },
  exclude: ({ file }) => file.stem === 'tmp'
});
```

### archive-creator

```js
// 1.x
archiveCreator({ format: 'zip', pluginOptions: { archiveName: 'site.zip' }, archiveOptions: { zlib: { level: 9 } } });

// 2.0: the format comes from the name's extension
archiveCreator({ name: 'site.zip', archiverOptions: { zlib: { level: 9 } } });
```

### scss-compiler and the minifiers

```js
// 1.x
scssCompiler({ scssOptions: { style: 'compressed' } });
jsSqueezer({ minifyOptions: { compress: { drop_console: true } } });
htmlSqueezer({}); // minified nothing without options

// 2.0
scssCompiler({ sassOptions: { style: 'compressed' } });
jsSqueezer({ terserOptions: { compress: { drop_console: true } } });
htmlSqueezer(); // the conservative preset; { preset: 'comprehensive' } for the smallest output
```

### A CommonJS gulpfile

1.x shipped a separate CommonJS build. 2.0 is ES modules only, which Node.js 22.13+ loads with `require()`; take the named export, since `require()` returns the module namespace:

```js
const { scssCompiler } = require('@zilero/gulp-scss-compiler');
```

## New in 2.0

[css-squeezer](/plugins/css-squeezer), [image-squeezer](/plugins/image-squeezer), [file-concat](/plugins/file-concat), [text-replace](/plugins/text-replace), [asset-revision](/plugins/asset-revision) and [file-changed](/plugins/file-changed).

url: /gulp-plugins-hub/plugins.md
---
# Plugins

Every plugin is its own package under the `@zilero` scope: install only what the build uses.

```sh
npm install --save-dev gulp @zilero/gulp-scss-compiler @zilero/gulp-css-squeezer
```

## Compile

| Plugin                                  | Does                                                                | Replaces  |
| --------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------- |
| [pug-compiler](/plugins/pug-compiler)   | Pug templates to HTML, with data per file; partials are skipped.    | gulp-pug  |
| [scss-compiler](/plugins/scss-compiler) | SCSS and indented Sass to CSS with sass-embedded, source maps kept. | gulp-sass |

## Optimize

| Plugin                                    | Does                                                                           | Replaces                          |
| ----------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------- |
| [html-squeezer](/plugins/html-squeezer)   | Minifies HTML with html-minifier-next presets.                                 | gulp-htmlmin                      |
| [css-squeezer](/plugins/css-squeezer)     | Minifies, prefixes and lowers CSS for your browsers with Lightning CSS.        | gulp-clean-css, gulp-autoprefixer |
| [js-squeezer](/plugins/js-squeezer)       | Minifies JavaScript with terser, source maps chained.                          | gulp-terser, gulp-uglify          |
| [image-squeezer](/plugins/image-squeezer) | Optimizes images, converts to WebP and AVIF, resizes for `srcset`, with sharp. | gulp-imagemin, gulp-webp          |
| [font-switcher](/plugins/font-switcher)   | Converts fonts to woff2, woff, ttf, eot and svg, with glyph subsetting.        | gulp-ttf2woff2, gulp-fontmin      |

## Transform

| Plugin                                      | Does                                                                           | Replaces                   |
| ------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------- |
| [file-concat](/plugins/file-concat)         | Joins files into one, in the order you set, with a header and footer.          | gulp-concat, gulp-header   |
| [text-replace](/plugins/text-replace)       | Replaces text with strings, regular expressions or async functions.            | gulp-replace, gulp-header  |
| [refilename](/plugins/refilename)           | Renames files: a name, a prefix or suffix, an extension, a folder, a function. | gulp-rename                |
| [asset-revision](/plugins/asset-revision)   | Content hashes in asset names, references rewritten, a manifest.               | gulp-rev, gulp-rev-rewrite |
| [archive-creator](/plugins/archive-creator) | Packs the stream into a zip, tar or tar.gz archive.                            | gulp-zip, gulp-tar         |

## Route and filter

| Plugin                                | Does                                                                   | Replaces                 |
| ------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------ |
| [conditional](/plugins/conditional)   | Sends each file through the first branch whose condition holds for it. | gulp-if                  |
| [file-exclude](/plugins/file-exclude) | Drops files by glob, regular expression, size or predicate.            | gulp-filter, gulp-ignore |
| [file-changed](/plugins/file-changed) | Lets through only the files that changed since the last build.         | gulp-changed, gulp-newer |
| [folder-clone](/plugins/folder-clone) | Copies every file into extra folders in one pass.                      | gulp-clone               |

All of them are built with the [plugin factory](/guide/writing-plugins), which you can use for your own.

---
url: /gulp-plugins-hub/plugins/pug-compiler.md
description: >-
  Render Pug templates to HTML in a gulp stream, with locals from options or
  file.data and partials skipped.
---

# pug-compiler

Renders Pug templates to HTML from the file contents, so earlier plugins can change them. Locals come from `file.data` and an object or a function of each file, includes and `extends` resolve from the file's own path, and partials such as `_layout.pug` are dropped.

```sh
npm install --save-dev @zilero/gulp-pug-compiler
```

## Usage

```js
import { dest, src } from 'gulp';
import pugCompiler from '@zilero/gulp-pug-compiler';

export const pages = () =>
  src('src/**/*.pug')
    .pipe(pugCompiler({ data: { year: 2026 }, pugOptions: { pretty: true } })) // index.pug → index.html
    .pipe(dest('dist'));
```

`data` can be a function that returns the locals for each file, the output can have another extension, and `onBeforeCompile` changes the template before pug sees it:

```js
pugCompiler({ data: async ({ file }) => ({ page: file.stem }) }); // front matter, a JSON file next to it, …
pugCompiler({ extname: '.php' }); // index.pug → index.php
pugCompiler({ onBeforeCompile: ({ content }) => content.replaceAll('{{year}}', '2026') });
```

## Options

| Option            | Type                                                | Default   | Description                                                                                                                     |
| ----------------- | --------------------------------------------------- | --------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `pugOptions`      | `Options`                                           | —         | Passed to pug as an object: `pretty`, `doctype`, `filters`, `basedir`, … `filename` is set by the plugin.                       |
| `data`            | `object \| ({ file }) => object \| Promise<object>` | —         | Locals for every template, or a function that returns them for each file. Merged over `file.data`: these win.                   |
| `extname`         | `string`                                            | `'.html'` | The extension of the output, with its dot.                                                                                      |
| `skipPartials`    | `boolean`                                           | `true`    | Drop partials instead of rendering them: files whose name, or the name of a folder they are in below the base, starts with `_`. |
| `onBeforeCompile` | `({ content, file }) => string \| Promise<string>`  | —         | Runs on the template source before pug and returns the source to compile. The file still has its own extension.                 |
| `onAfterCompile`  | `({ content, file }) => string \| Promise<string>`  | —         | Runs on the rendered HTML and returns the final HTML. The file already has its new extension.                                   |

Unknown keys, an extension without its dot such as `'html'`, a `data` that is neither an object nor a function and a `pugOptions` that is not an object are an error when the plugin is created.

## Locals

A template is rendered with `file.data`, then `data` over it: the object, or what the function returns for the file. On a key both have, the option wins. `file.data` is the convention of [gulp-data](https://www.npmjs.com/package/gulp-data) and front-matter plugins, and is used when it is a plain object.

```js
import data from 'gulp-data';

export const pages = () =>
  src('src/pages/**/*.pug')
    .pipe(data((file) => ({ title: file.stem }))) // file.data
    .pipe(pugCompiler({ data: { siteName: 'Example' } })) // title and siteName
    .pipe(dest('dist'));
```

## Hooks

`onBeforeCompile` and `onAfterCompile` get `{ content, file }` and return the text to continue with, or a promise of it. A hook that returns anything else, say a JavaScript hook that forgets its `return`, fails the file with `onAfterCompile must return the text as a string, got undefined`. The `data` function gets `{ file }`, typed `TemplateDataInput`. The types are exported from the package: `ContentHook`, `ContentHookInput`, `TemplateData`, `TemplateDataFunction`, `TemplateDataInput`.

## Notes

* Only `.pug` and `.jade` files are rendered, in any case. Other files, and files without contents (`read: false`), pass through untouched.
* Relative includes and `extends` resolve from the file's path. Absolute ones (`include /templates/_nav.pug`) resolve from `basedir`, which defaults to `file.base`: the folder before the first glob in `src()`.
* With `skipPartials`, partials leave the stream, so they are not written to `dest`; templates still include them from disk. A partial is a file whose name starts with `_` (`_layout.pug`) or that sits in a folder whose name does, below `file.base` (`_includes/nav.pug`, `_layouts/base.pug`).
* No source maps are produced. A file that already has one (`src(…, { sourcemaps: true })`) keeps it, with `sourceMap.file` following the new extension.
* An error from pug, `data` or a hook, such as a template pug cannot compile or render, emits a PluginError with the file path.
* Templates are compiled with `compileDebug: true`, so an error while rendering quotes the lines of the compiled text, the contents as earlier plugins left them, instead of reading the file from disk. Set `pugOptions: { compileDebug: false }` to turn it off.
* The compiler is [pug](https://pugjs.org) 3; its options go through `pugOptions`.

## Migrating

### From gulp-pug

| gulp-pug                                | pug-compiler                                          |
| --------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| `pug({ pretty, doctype, … })`           | `pugCompiler({ pugOptions: { pretty, doctype, … } })` |
| `data`, `locals`                        | `data`, an object or a function of the file           |
| `file.data` wins over `data`/`locals`   | `data` wins over `file.data`                          |
| `client: true` (compile to functions)   | not supported                                         |
| `pug` (your own pug instance), `jade`   | not supported: pug 3 is built in                      |
| `verbose`                               | not supported                                         |
| renders every `.pug` file, partials too | partials dropped; `skipPartials: false` keeps them    |

### From 1.x

* 1.x compiled the file from disk with `compileFile`, ignoring changes made by earlier plugins. Now the file contents are compiled.
* `data` is new: locals as an object or a function of the file.
* `extname` is new; the default stays `.html`.
* Partials (`_*.pug`) are dropped by default; 1.x rendered every `.pug` file, partials included. `skipPartials: false` keeps them.
* `onAfterCompile` moved from `pluginOptions` to the top level and gets `{ content, file }`.
* `onBeforeCompile` is new: it changes the template source before pug.
* `basedir` defaults to `file.base`, so absolute includes work without options.

See [migrating from 1.x](/guide/migration) for every package.
