---
url: /gulp-plugins-hub/plugins/archive-creator.md
description: >-
  Pack the files of a gulp stream into one reproducible zip, tar or tar.gz
  archive with archiver.
---

# archive-creator

Packs every file of the stream into one zip, tar or tar.gz archive with archiver and emits only the archive. Entries keep their paths relative to `file.base`, and their modification time and mode when the files came from disk. The archive is built in memory.

```sh
npm install --save-dev @zilero/gulp-archive-creator
```

## Usage

```js
import { dest, src } from 'gulp';
import archiveCreator from '@zilero/gulp-archive-creator';

export const release = () =>
  src('dist/**', { encoding: false })
    .pipe(archiveCreator({ name: 'site.zip' }))
    .pipe(dest('releases'));
```

The format comes from the name, or from `format`:

```js
archiveCreator({ name: 'site.tar.gz' }); // tgz, from the extension
archiveCreator({ name: 'releases/site', format: 'tgz' }); // releases/site.tar.gz
archiveCreator({ name: 'site.zip', archiverOptions: { zlib: { level: 9 } } }); // passed to archiver
```

## Options

| Option            | Type                      | Default     | Description                                                                                                                           |
| ----------------- | ------------------------- | ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `name`            | `string`                  | `'archive'` | The archive's path relative to the output folder: `site.zip`, `releases/site.tar.gz`. Without an extension the format's own is added. |
| `format`          | `'zip' \| 'tar' \| 'tgz'` | from `name` | Inferred from the extension of `name` (`.zip`, `.tar`, `.tgz`, `.tar.gz`), else zip. When both are given they must agree.             |
| `archiverOptions` | `ZipOptions & TarOptions` | —           | Passed to archiver: `zlib.level` or `store` for zip, `gzipOptions` for tgz. Must be an object (`Expected an object`).                 |
| `emptyArchive`    | `boolean`                 | `false`     | Emit an empty archive when the stream had no files. By default nothing is emitted.                                                    |
| `directories`     | `boolean`                 | `false`     | Add an entry for each directory in the stream (`src('**')` without `nodir`).                                                          |
| `modifiedTime`    | `Date`                    | —           | The modification time of every entry, for reproducible archives. Default: each file's `stat.mtime`, else 1980-01-01.                  |

All options are optional, and unknown keys are an error. `name` must stay inside the output folder: an absolute path or one that leaves it, such as `'../site.zip'`, is an error (`Expected a path inside the output folder`). So is a `format` that contradicts the extension of `name`: `{ name: 'a.zip', format: 'tar' }` throws `a.zip is a zip name, but format is tar: change one of them or drop format`. Options are checked when the plugin is created.

The package also exports the types `ArchiveCreatorOptions`, `ArchiveFormat` and `ArchiverOptions`.

## Notes

* Read files with `src(…, { encoding: false })`: gulp 5 reads files as UTF-8 by default, which breaks images, fonts and other binary files.
* The archive is placed relative to the `base` of the first file, so `dest('releases')` writes `releases/site.zip`.
* `format` is useful with a name without a known extension (`{ name: 'releases/site', format: 'tgz' }` writes `releases/site.tar.gz`); with a known extension it must agree with it. Extensions are matched case-insensitively.
* The archive is built in memory: every entry is compressed into a Buffer that is emitted at the end of the stream, so the archive must fit in memory. Streamed contents (`buffer: false`) are read entry by entry, but the result is still one Buffer.
* Files read with `buffer: false` are archived from their stream.
* Files without contents that are not directories (`read: false`, symbolic links) are skipped. Directories are skipped too unless `directories` is set. With `directories`, the base folder itself (`src('dist')` matches `dist` with an empty relative path) gets no entry, since it has no path inside the archive.
* An error while reading streamed contents, or an error from archiver, fails the task with a `PluginError` named after this plugin; it is reported on the next file or at the end of the stream, and the process does not crash. archiver's warnings (a missing file, for example) fail the archive the same way rather than being ignored. After a failure, archiver is aborted, so the remaining entries are not read.
* An empty stream emits nothing unless `emptyArchive` is set; the empty archive is then named relative to the current folder.

## Reproducible archives

The same files give the same archive on every build, byte for byte, as long as the dates are stable:

* files read from disk keep their `stat.mtime`, so they change the archive only when they change;
* files without a stat (made by other plugins, such as a concatenated bundle) get a fixed 1980-01-01, the earliest date zip can store, instead of the time of the build;
* `modifiedTime` gives every entry the same date, ignoring `stat.mtime`, for archives that depend only on the contents (CI builds from a fresh checkout, where every mtime is the checkout time).

zip stores dates in local time, so a zip is reproducible across machines in the same time zone; tar stores UTC.

```js
archiveCreator({ name: 'site.tar.gz', modifiedTime: new Date('2026-01-01T00:00:00Z') });
```

## Migrating

### From gulp-zip, gulp-tar and gulp-gzip

| gulp-zip, gulp-tar + gulp-gzip   | archive-creator                           |
| -------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
| `zip('site.zip')`                | `archiveCreator({ name: 'site.zip' })`    |
| `zip(name, { compress: false })` | `archiverOptions: { store: true }`        |
| `zip(name, { modifiedTime })`    | `modifiedTime`                            |
| `zip(name, { buffer: false })`   | not needed: the archive is one Buffer     |
| `tar('site.tar')`, then `gzip()` | `archiveCreator({ name: 'site.tar.gz' })` |

### From 1.x

* Options are flat: `{ name, format, archiverOptions, emptyArchive, directories }` instead of `format`, `archiveOptions` and `pluginOptions: { archiveName, createDirectory, createEmptyArchive }`.
* `format` is no longer required: it is inferred from the extension of `name`.
* tar.gz (`tgz`) is supported.
* archiver 8 is used, streamed contents are supported and entries keep their modification time and mode.
* After 2.0.0: `modifiedTime` is new, files without a stat get a fixed date instead of the build time, and a `format` that contradicts the extension of `name` is an error (2.0.0 wrote a tar named `a.zip`).

See [migrating from 1.x](/guide/migration) for every package.

---
url: /gulp-plugins-hub/plugins/conditional.md
description: >-
  Route each file of a gulp stream through a different plugin chain by glob,
  RegExp or a function of the file, like if / else if / else for streams.
---

# conditional

Sends each file through the first branch whose condition holds for it, like if / else if / else for streams. A branch is any plugin or chain of plugins; files that no condition matches go to a default branch or pass through untouched.

```sh
npm install --save-dev @zilero/gulp-conditional
```

## Usage

```js
import { dest, src } from 'gulp';
import conditional from '@zilero/gulp-conditional';
import htmlSqueezer from '@zilero/gulp-html-squeezer';
import jsSqueezer from '@zilero/gulp-js-squeezer';

export const build = () =>
  src('src/**')
    .pipe(
      conditional({
        handlers: [
          { condition: '*.js', handler: () => jsSqueezer() },
          { condition: '*.html', handler: () => htmlSqueezer() }
        ]
      })
    )
    .pipe(dest('dist'));
```

A condition is a boolean, a glob, a RegExp, an array of globs and RegExps, or a function that gets `{ file }`; a function may be async:

```js
import conditional from '@zilero/gulp-conditional';
import jsSqueezer from '@zilero/gulp-js-squeezer';
import refilename from '@zilero/gulp-refilename';
import { stat } from 'node:fs/promises';

conditional({
  handlers: [
    // a boolean: in development every file goes here
    { condition: process.env.NODE_ENV !== 'production', handler: () => refilename({ suffix: '.dev' }) },
    // globs and RegExps match file.relative; a glob without a slash matches the name in any folder
    { condition: ['vendor/**', /\.min\.js$/], handler: () => refilename({ suffix: '.vendor' }) },
    // an async function of the file
    { condition: async ({ file }) => (await stat(file.path)).size > 50_000, handler: () => jsSqueezer() }
  ],
  // everything else
  defaultHandler: () => refilename({ suffix: '.min' })
});
```

A handler may return an array of streams. They form a chain: the files go through them in order, and an error from any stream of the chain is emitted.

```js
import conditional from '@zilero/gulp-conditional';
import cssSqueezer from '@zilero/gulp-css-squeezer';
import scssCompiler from '@zilero/gulp-scss-compiler';

conditional({
  handlers: [{ condition: ({ file }) => file.extname === '.scss', handler: () => [scssCompiler(), cssSqueezer()] }]
});
```

Return an array, not `a().pipe(b())`. `.pipe()` returns its argument, so the handler would hand back `b` alone: the files would be written into `b` and skip `a`, and an error from `a` would not reach the task.

## Options

| Option           | Type                       | Default | Description                                                                                                       |
| ---------------- | -------------------------- | ------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `handlers`       | `{ condition, handler }[]` | none    | Branches, checked in order for every file; the first one whose condition holds gets it. At least one is required. |
| `defaultHandler` | `() => Duplex \| Duplex[]` | none    | Creates the stream, or the chain, for the files no condition matched. Without it they pass through untouched.     |

Each branch in `handlers`:

| Key         | Type                                                                                               | Description                                                                                                                      |
| ----------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `condition` | `boolean \| string \| RegExp \| (string \| RegExp)[] \| ({ file }) => boolean \| Promise<boolean>` | `true`, a glob or RegExp that matches `file.relative` (any of an array), or a function that returns `true`, sends the file here. |
| `handler`   | `() => Duplex \| Duplex[]`                                                                         | Creates the stream the matching files go through, or a non-empty array of streams to go through in order.                        |

Unknown keys are an error, and so are an empty `handlers` array (`Add at least one handler`), an empty glob and a condition of any other type (`Expected a boolean, a glob, a RegExp, an array of globs or a function`). Options are checked when the plugin is created.

A handler is checked when its first file arrives. One that returns something other than a stream, or an array with something else in it, emits `handlers[0].handler must return a stream or an array of streams, got undefined` (`defaultHandler …` for the default branch): a handler that forgets `return`, or returns the plugin function instead of calling it, is caught there. An empty array emits `handlers[0].handler returned an empty array; return at least one stream`. Streams are recognized by shape (`write`, `pipe`, `on`), so plugins built on `readable-stream` or `through2` work.

Globs are matched with picomatch against `file.relative` with `/` separators, dotfiles included: a glob without a slash matches the file name in any folder (`'*.js'`), one with a slash matches the whole relative path (`'scripts/**'`). A global or sticky RegExp is reset before every file. Globs and RegExps are compiled once, when the plugin is created.

The package also exports the types `ConditionalOptions`, `ConditionalBranch`, `Condition`, `ConditionFunction`, `PathPattern`, `BranchHandler` and `BranchStream`.

## Notes

* Conditions are checked for every file, in the order of `handlers`; later conditions are not called once one holds.
* Each branch is created once, for the first file that goes to it. A branch that gets no files is never created.
* The stream ends after every branch has finished, so branches that emit files when they end (a concat or a bundle) work.
* Branches run side by side: files from different branches can come out in a different order than they went in.
* A slow branch slows the stream down: files wait until the branch can take more.
* A branch's output is not throttled by the downstream: what it emits is pushed on at once. A branch that emits a very large number of files, or very large ones, can hold them all in memory while a slow downstream catches up.
* A thrown condition fails the task with a `PluginError` named after this plugin.
* An error from a branch is reported on the next file written to the conditional stream, or at the end of the stream, where it is the same `PluginError` whichever way the branch's failure is noticed. A branch that fails while a condition is being awaited fails the stream too, instead of leaving it hanging. A `PluginError` keeps the name of the plugin that threw it, and any other error is wrapped in a `PluginError` named after this plugin when it happens, so it is not attributed to the file processed next.
* When the conditional ends, fails or is destroyed, every branch stream is destroyed with it, so no branch (a Sass compiler, for example) keeps the process alive.
* Every file goes through the conditions, including files without contents and directories.

## Migrating

### From gulp-if

| gulp-if                               | conditional                                                               |
| ------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `gulpIf(condition, uglify())`         | `conditional({ handlers: [{ condition, handler: () => jsSqueezer() }] })` |
| `gulpIf(condition, a(), b())` (else)  | `handlers: [{ condition, handler: a }]`, `defaultHandler: b`              |
| nested `gulpIf` for else-if           | more entries in `handlers`, checked in order                              |
| a lazy pipe of plugins for a chain    | return an array: `handler: () => [a(), b()]`                              |
| a glob string, a function of the file | the same; globs match `file.relative`, RegExps and arrays work too        |

The branch is created by a function (`handler: () => plugin()`) rather than passed in, so it only exists once a file needs it, and it is destroyed with the conditional.

### From 1.x

* Conditions are now checked for every file. In 1.x a condition was evaluated once when the plugin was created, and the whole stream went to one handler.
* A condition may be a function of the file (`({ file }) => …`), sync or async, a glob, a RegExp or an array of them, as well as a boolean.
* A handler may return an array of streams to chain.
* Branches are created only when a file goes to them, and files that match nothing pass through when there is no `defaultHandler`.
* Files from different branches may interleave.

See [migrating from 1.x](/guide/migration) for every package.

---

---
url: /gulp-plugins-hub/plugins/file-exclude.md
description: >-
  Drop files from a gulp stream by glob, regular expression, size or your own
  predicate, or keep only the matching ones with invert.
---

# file-exclude

Drops files from the stream: those that match a glob or regular expression, fall outside a size range or that your own check rejects. Every other file passes through untouched. With `invert: true` it keeps only those files instead.

```sh
npm install --save-dev @zilero/gulp-file-exclude
```

## Usage

```js
import { dest, src } from 'gulp';
import fileExclude from '@zilero/gulp-file-exclude';

export const copy = () =>
  src('src/**', { encoding: false })
    .pipe(fileExclude({ patterns: ['*.map', 'drafts/**'], size: { max: 1024 * 1024 } }))
    .pipe(dest('dist'));
```

The rules can be combined; a file is dropped as soon as one of them matches:

```js
fileExclude({ patterns: '*.map' }); // every source map, in any folder
fileExclude({ patterns: [/^drafts\//, /\.psd$/] }); // regular expressions on the relative path
fileExclude({ size: { min: 1 } }); // empty files
fileExclude({ exclude: ({ file }) => file.stem.startsWith('_') }); // your own check
fileExclude({ patterns: ['*.png', '*.jpg'], invert: true }); // keep only images
```

`invert` turns the plugin into a filter that keeps what the rules match, like gulp-filter: the rules run as usual, and a file is kept when one of them matches and dropped otherwise. gulp-filter's `restore` (process some files, then put the others back) has no counterpart here: use [conditional](/plugins/conditional), which sends the matching files through a branch while the rest pass through.

## Options

| Option     | Type                                        | Default | Description                                                                                                                          |
| ---------- | ------------------------------------------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `patterns` | `string \| RegExp \| (string \| RegExp)[]`  | none    | Globs (picomatch) or regular expressions matched against the path relative to `file.base`. An array needs at least one pattern.      |
| `size`     | `{ min?: number, max?: number }`            | none    | Drops files smaller than `min` or larger than `max` bytes. Both are non-negative integers, and `min` must not be greater than `max`. |
| `exclude`  | `({ file }) => boolean \| Promise<boolean>` | none    | Your own check, run after `patterns` and `size`: it gets one object with the Vinyl `file`; return `true` to drop the file.           |
| `invert`   | `boolean`                                   | `false` | Keep only the files a rule matches (`patterns`, `size` or `exclude`) and drop the rest.                                              |

Set at least one of `patterns`, `size` or `exclude` (`invert` alone is not a rule): options that exclude nothing are an error (`Set at least one of patterns, size or exclude`), and so is an empty `patterns` array (`Add at least one pattern`) or an empty glob. Unknown keys are an error too. Options are checked when the plugin is created.

Some globs are rejected rather than matched in a way you might not expect:

| Glob                       | Error                                                                                         | Why                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| -------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `'!*.css'`                 | `Negated globs are not supported: list what to drop, or set invert to keep only what matches` | In gulp-filter a `!` glob means "keep", here every pattern means "drop". List the files to drop instead, or list the files to keep and set `invert: true`: `{ patterns: '*.css', invert: true }`. |
| `'drafts\\**'`             | `Expected / in globs, not \`                                                                  | Paths are matched with `/` separators on every platform, and `\` in a glob is an escape, so a Windows-style glob would never match.                                                               |
| `'/home/me/src/drafts/**'` | `Expected a glob relative to file.base, not an absolute path`                                 | Patterns are matched against `file.relative`, so an absolute glob would never match. Write it relative to the glob base of `src()`: `'drafts/**'`.                                                |

Regular expressions are not checked this way: they are tested as they are.

The package also exports the types `FileExcludeOptions`, `ExcludePredicate` and `SizeRange`.

## Notes

* Paths use `/` separators on every platform, so the same patterns work on Windows.
* A glob without a slash matches the file name in any folder: `*.map` drops `app.js.map` and `js/vendor.js.map`. A glob with a slash matches the whole relative path: `drafts/**`, `img/*.png`.
* Globs match dotfiles: `img/*.png` also drops `img/.hidden.png`.
* Regular expressions are tested against the relative path, not only the name: use `/\.png$/` or `/^drafts\//`. A global (`g`) or sticky (`y`) RegExp works too: its `lastIndex` is reset before every file, so each test starts at the beginning of the path.
* `size` uses the length of the contents, or the size on disk (`file.stat.size`) for files without Buffer contents (`read: false`, streamed contents). Directories are never dropped by `size`, and neither are files of unknown size (no contents and no `stat`).
* The rules run in order (patterns, size, then `exclude`), so `exclude` only sees the files the first two kept.

## Migrating

### From gulp-filter and gulp-ignore

| gulp-filter / gulp-ignore                        | file-exclude                                                    |
| ------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `filter(['**/*.js'])` (keep matching)            | `fileExclude({ patterns: '*.js', invert: true })`               |
| `filter(['**', '!**/*.map'])`                    | `fileExclude({ patterns: '*.map' })`                            |
| `filter(pattern, { restore: true })` + `restore` | [conditional](/plugins/conditional) with a branch for the files |
| `ignore.exclude(condition)`                      | `fileExclude({ patterns })` or `fileExclude({ exclude })`       |
| `ignore.include(condition)`                      | the same with `invert: true`                                    |

### From 1.x

* A string in `patterns` is now a glob on the relative path, not a substring of the file name: replace `'.map'` with `'*.map'`.
* `size` is now `{ min, max }` instead of a `[min, max]` tuple; either bound can be left out.
* `onExclude` is renamed `exclude`; it gets `{ file }` instead of the file, and it may return a boolean as well as a promise.
* At least one rule is required.
* `invert` is new: it keeps only the matching files.

See [migrating from 1.x](/guide/migration) for every package.

---

---
url: /gulp-plugins-hub/plugins/file-changed.md
description: >-
  A gulp plugin that passes only the files changed since the last build, by
  modification time or contents, with extra dependencies such as Sass partials.
---

# file-changed

Lets through only the files that changed since the last build: the built file in the destination is missing, older or different. Put it right after `src` so a watch build skips the rest of the pipeline for untouched files.

```sh
npm install --save-dev @zilero/gulp-file-changed
```

## Usage

```js
import { dest, src } from 'gulp';
import fileChanged from '@zilero/gulp-file-changed';
import imageSqueezer from '@zilero/gulp-image-squeezer';

export const images = () =>
  src('src/images/**', { encoding: false })
    .pipe(fileChanged({ dest: 'dist/images' }))
    .pipe(imageSqueezer())
    .pipe(dest('dist/images'));
```

When the build renames files, tell the plugin where the built file is:

```js
fileChanged({ dest: 'dist/css', extname: '.css' }); // main.scss → dist/css/main.css
fileChanged({ dest: 'dist', target: ({ file }) => `images/${file.stem}-1280w.jpg` }); // any other name
fileChanged({ dest: 'dist', compare: 'contents' }); // for builds that copy files as they are
```

When every file depends on others the stream does not carry (Sass partials, a shared config), list them in `extra`: a file then also passes when the newest of them is newer than its built file.

```js
fileChanged({ dest: 'dist/css', extname: '.css', extra: ['src/scss/**/_*.scss', 'browserslist'] });
```

## Options

| Option    | Type                                                     | Default   | Description                                                                                                                                        |
| --------- | -------------------------------------------------------- | --------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `dest`    | `string \| ({ file }) => string`                         | —         | The folder `dest` writes to, relative to `file.cwd` or absolute: the same value, or a function of the file. Required.                              |
| `extname` | `string`                                                 | —         | The extension the built file has, when the build changes it: `.css` for `.scss` sources. With its dot: `'css'` is an error.                        |
| `target`  | `({ file }) => string`                                   | —         | The built file's path, relative to `dest` or absolute, for builds that rename files in other ways. Wins over `extname`: `extname` is then ignored. |
| `extra`   | `string \| string[]`                                     | —         | Globs, relative to `file.cwd`, of files every file depends on. When the newest of them is newer than a file's built file, the file passes.         |
| `compare` | `'mtime' \| 'contents' \| ({ file, target }) => boolean` | `'mtime'` | How a file counts as changed. See below.                                                                                                           |

`dest` and `target` are called once per file and must return a string, not a promise. `target` gets one object with the Vinyl `file`; a relative path it returns is resolved against `dest`, and an absolute one is used as it is:

```js
import path from 'node:path';

fileChanged({ dest: 'dist', target: ({ file }) => `pages/${file.stem}/index.html` }); // dist/pages/about/index.html
fileChanged({ dest: 'dist', target: ({ file }) => path.resolve('cache', `${file.stem}.json`) }); // outside dest
```

`compare` can be:

| Value        | A file is changed when                                                                     |
| ------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `'mtime'`    | It is newer than the built file, in whole milliseconds.                                    |
| `'contents'` | Its bytes differ from the built file. Only for builds that copy files as they are.         |
| a function   | It returns `true` (or a promise of `true`); it gets the file and `target: { path, stat }`. |

`'contents'` fits only builds that write each file unchanged (copying static files, fonts, already optimized images). When the pipeline changes the file (compiles, minifies, adds a banner), the built file never has the source's bytes, so every file counts as changed on every run: use `'mtime'` there.

Unknown keys are an error. Options are checked when the plugin is created.

The package also exports the types `FileChangedOptions`, `CompareFunction`, `CompareInput`, `CompareMode`, `DestResolver` and `TargetResolver`.

## Notes

* Without `extname` or `target`, the built file is `dest` plus the path relative to `file.base`: `src/css/main.css` with `dest: 'dist'` is compared with `dist/css/main.css`.
* Files that were never built always pass, and so do directories. A `dest` (or `target`) that points at a file where a folder is expected counts as never built too.
* `extra` is checked after the built file is found and before `compare`: when the newest file the globs match is newer than the built file (in whole milliseconds), the file passes whatever `compare` says. Globs that match nothing are ignored. They are resolved once per stream (once per watch run, since gulp creates a new stream each time), relative to `file.cwd` (globs by [tinyglobby](https://github.com/SuperchupuDev/tinyglobby), dot-files included).
* `'mtime'` compares whole milliseconds: `dest` writes modification times with millisecond precision, so the sub-millisecond fraction a source keeps would otherwise make every file look newer than its built copy.
* With `'mtime'`, files without a `stat` always pass. With `'contents'`, files without buffered contents (`buffer: false`, `read: false`) always pass.
* Files that did not change are dropped; the others pass through untouched.
* Only a missing built file (or a file where a folder is expected) counts as never built. Any other error while checking it, such as a permission error, fails the task with a `PluginError`; so does an error thrown by a `dest`, `target` or `compare` function.
* Not for plugins that combine files (concat, archives): they need every file, not only the changed ones.

## Migrating

### From gulp-changed and gulp-newer

| gulp-changed / gulp-newer                                        | file-changed                                 |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
| `changed('dist')`, `newer('dist')`                               | `fileChanged({ dest: 'dist' })`              |
| `changed(dest, { extension: '.css' })`, `newer({ ext: '.css' })` | `extname: '.css'`                            |
| `transformPath`, `newer({ map })`                                | `target: ({ file }) => path`                 |
| `hasChanged: changed.compareContents`                            | `compare: 'contents'`                        |
| `hasChanged: changed.compareLastModifiedTime`                    | `compare: 'mtime'` (the default)             |
| a custom `hasChanged`                                            | `compare: ({ file, target }) => boolean`     |
| `newer({ extra })`                                               | `extra`                                      |
| `newer('dist/bundle.js')` (many sources, one file)               | not supported: run concat-like tasks in full |

### From 1.x

file-changed is new in 2.0; there was no 1.x.

---

---
url: /gulp-plugins-hub/plugins/folder-clone.md
description: >-
  Copy every file of a gulp stream into one or more extra folders in a single
  pass, with a hook to change, replace or skip each copy.
---

# folder-clone

Copies every file of the stream into one or more extra folders, relative to `file.base`, so a single `dest` writes them all. The originals are kept unless you turn them off, and a hook can change, replace or skip each copy. It replaces gulp-clone and the second `dest` that goes with it.

```sh
npm install --save-dev @zilero/gulp-folder-clone
```

## Usage

```ts
import { folderClone } from '@zilero/gulp-folder-clone';
import { dest, src } from 'gulp';
import { pipeline } from 'node:stream/promises';

// dist/images/logo.png, dist/backup/images/logo.png and dist/v2/images/logo.png
export const images = (): Promise<void> =>
  pipeline(
    src('src/images/**', { base: 'src', encoding: false }),
    folderClone({ dirs: ['backup', 'v2'] }),
    dest('dist')
  );
```

`onClone` runs for every copy:

```ts
folderClone({
  dirs: ['legacy', 'drafts'],
  onClone: ({ file, dir, original }) => {
    if (dir === 'drafts') {
      return null; // skip this copy
    }

    file.stem = `${file.stem}-${dir}`; // change it in place
  }
});
```

## Options

| Option         | Type                                                                                   | Default | Description                                                                                       |
| -------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `dirs`         | `string \| string[]`                                                                   | —       | One or more folders inside `file.base` that receive a copy of every file. Required.               |
| `keepOriginal` | `boolean`                                                                              | `true`  | Emit the original file as well as the copies.                                                     |
| `onClone`      | `({ file, dir, original }) => Vinyl \| null \| void \| Promise<Vinyl \| null \| void>` | —       | Runs for every copy, may be async: change it in place, return another file, or `null` to skip it. |

`onClone` gets:

| Key        | Description                                             |
| ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------- |
| `file`     | The copy, already moved into `dir`; change it in place. |
| `dir`      | The folder this copy goes to, as given in `dirs`.       |
| `original` | The file the copy was made from.                        |

Return nothing to keep the copy, `null` to skip it, or another Vinyl file to emit instead. The source map of the emitted file is pointed at its path after the hook, so a copy the hook renames or moves keeps a correct map.

Each folder in `dirs` must be a relative path inside `file.base`: an absolute path, `'.'` (the base itself), a path that leaves the base such as `'../out'`, and an empty string are errors, and so is an empty `dirs` list (`Add at least one folder`). A folder listed twice, also written differently (`'backup'` and `'./backup/'`), is an error (`Each folder may be listed only once`): both copies would be written to the same path. Unknown keys are an error too. Options are checked when the plugin is created.

The package also exports the types `FolderCloneOptions`, `CloneHook` and `CloneInput`.

## Notes

* A copy keeps the original's `base` and gets the path `base/dir/relative`: `img/logo.png` with `dirs: 'backup'` becomes `backup/img/logo.png`.
* Copies are deep clones: each has its own contents and its own source map object, so changing a copy never touches the original or another copy.
* With `src(…, { sourcemaps: true })`, each copy's `sourceMap.file` points at the copy's relative path, after `onClone`; the original's map is left as it was.
* For each file the original comes first, then one copy per folder in the order of `dirs`. With `keepOriginal: false` and every copy skipped, nothing is emitted for that file.
* Every file is cloned, including files without contents (`read: false`) and directories.
* Read images and other binary files with `src(…, { encoding: false })`; gulp 5 reads files as UTF-8 by default.
* An error thrown by `onClone` is emitted as a `PluginError` with the file's path.

## Recipes

Mirror the build into `dist/latest`:

```ts
pipeline(src('dist/**', { encoding: false }), folderClone({ dirs: 'latest' }), dest('dist'));
```

Publish into two release folders, without the original:

```ts
folderClone({ dirs: ['releases/stable', 'releases/next'], keepOriginal: false });
```

Leave source maps out of one folder:

```ts
folderClone({
  dirs: 'public',
  onClone: ({ file }) => (file.extname === '.map' ? null : undefined)
});
```

## Migrating

### From gulp-clone

| gulp-clone                                                      | folder-clone                           |
| --------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------- |
| `clone()` / `clone.sink()`, a second branch with its own `dest` | `folderClone({ dirs })` and one `dest` |
| change the cloned files in the second branch                    | `onClone({ file, dir, original })`     |
| drop the originals by not writing the first branch              | `keepOriginal: false`                  |

### From 1.x

* 1.x only had an `onBeforeCopy(file)` hook and passed files through unchanged. 2.0 really copies each file into the folders in `dirs`.
* `keepOriginal` (default `true`) is new.
* `onBeforeCopy` is replaced by `onClone({ file, dir, original })`, which can change, replace or skip (`null`) each copy.

See [migrating from 1.x](/guide/migration) for every package.

---

description: >-
  API reference of @zilero/gulp-plugin-factory: createPlugin, parseOptions,
  hooks, source map, path and binary helpers.
---

# Plugin factory

`@zilero/gulp-plugin-factory` — the toolkit every plugin of the hub is built with. A guided tour is in [Writing a plugin](/guide/writing-plugins).

```ts
import {
  applySourceMap,
  assertBinaryContents,
  createPathMatcher,
  createPlugin,
  getChainableSourceMap,
  getInputSourceMap,
  isFunction,
  isObject,
  isRelativePathInside,
  isUrl,
  parseOptions,
  PluginError,
  runContentHook,
  syncSourceMapFile,
  toPluginError,
  toPosixPath,
  Vinyl
} from '@zilero/gulp-plugin-factory';
```

## `createPlugin(definition)`

Returns an object-mode `Transform` stream: Vinyl files in, Vinyl files out, one at a time and in order.

| Field        | Type                                                             | Description                                                                                                     |
| ------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `name`       | `string`                                                         | Prefixes every error; use the package name.                                                                     |
| `accept`     | `'buffer' \| 'any'`                                              | `'buffer'` (default): `transform` gets files with Buffer contents only. `'any'`: every file.                    |
| `extensions` | `readonly string[]`                                              | Only files with one of these extensions (`'.css'`, compared in lowercase) are transformed; others pass through. |
| `filter`     | `(file: Vinyl) => boolean`                                       | Files it returns false for pass through untouched, before any other check. Checked together with `extensions`.  |
| `binary`     | `boolean`                                                        | `accept: 'buffer'` only: files read as UTF-8 text emit the `assertBinaryContents` error before `transform`.     |
| `transform`  | `(file, context) => TransformResult \| Promise<TransformResult>` | Called for each file. Nothing: the file goes on. `null`: dropped. A file or an array: those go on instead.      |
| `flush`      | `(context) => void \| Promise<void>`                             | Runs once after the last file, before the stream ends.                                                          |
| `dispose`    | `() => void \| Promise<void>`                                    | Runs once when the stream is done: ended, failed or destroyed. Closes what the plugin opened.                   |

`context` is `{ name, push }`: `push(file)` sends a file downstream from `transform` or `flush`.

A `filter` that throws is reported like any other error. With `accept: 'buffer'`, a file without contents passes through and a file with streamed contents emits `Streaming is not supported`. Anything `transform` or `flush` throws or rejects with is emitted as a `PluginError` with the plugin name and the file path (`fileName`); a `PluginError` is emitted as it is.

Types: `PluginDefinition`, `BufferPluginDefinition`, `AnyPluginDefinition`, `PluginContext`, `TransformResult`, `BufferFile` (a Vinyl file whose `contents` is a `Buffer`), `PluginStream`.

## `parseOptions({ name, schema, options })`

Validates `options` against a synchronous [Standard Schema](https://standardschema.dev) (zod 4, valibot, arktype, …) and returns the parsed value, defaults applied. Invalid options throw a `PluginError`:

```text
Invalid options:
    • quality: Too big: expected number to be <=100
    • Unrecognized key: "qualty"
```

An asynchronous schema throws `The options schema must be synchronous`.

## `runContentHook({ name, hook, content, file })`

Runs an optional `ContentHook` and resolves with the text it returns; without a hook, resolves with `content`. A result that is not a string throws `<name> must return the text as a string, got <type>` (`name` is the option name, such as `'onAfterMinify'`), where a JavaScript hook that forgot to return would otherwise end as an obscure `Buffer.from(undefined)` error.

## `applySourceMap({ file, map, chain? })`

Stores a tool's source map (an object or JSON) as `file.sourceMap`, the way `dest(…, { sourcemaps })` expects it: `file` becomes the file's relative path, absolute or `file://` sources become relative to `file.base`, and every source uses `/`. With `chain: true` the file's current map is chained into the new one first, for tools that cannot take an input map. Only the sources that are the file itself get its map; other sources (an inlined import) stay as they are.

## `syncSourceMapFile(file)`

Sets `file.sourceMap.file` to the file's current relative path, with `/`. Call it after renaming or moving a file, so `dest` writes the map for the new name. Files without a map are left alone.

## `getChainableSourceMap(file)`

The file's map with absolute sources as `file://` URLs (`sourceRoot` applied; sources that are already URLs are kept), ready to chain into another map with `@jridgewell/remapping`; gulp keeps sources relative to `file.base`, while remapping resolves them against the map they are chained into. `undefined` when there is nothing to chain.

## `getInputSourceMap(file)`

The file's current map as JSON, to pass to a tool as its input map. `undefined` when the file has none, or has the empty map `src(…, { sourcemaps: true })` gives files without one: chaining that would leave the output map empty.

## `assertBinaryContents({ relative, contents })`

Throws when binary contents look like they were decoded as UTF-8 (the U+FFFD replacement character in the first 64 bytes), with the fix in the message: `` Read binary files with `src(globs, { encoding: false })` ``. `createPlugin({ binary: true })` calls it before `transform`.

## `createPathMatcher({ patterns, ignoreCase })`

Takes `patterns`, a `(string | RegExp)[]`, and returns `(relativePath: string) => boolean`, one test for every pattern. Globs go through picomatch with dotfiles included: a glob without `/` (`*.map`) matches the file name in any folder, a glob with `/` (`vendor/**`) matches from the base. A RegExp tests the path with `/` separators, from the start every time even when it is global or sticky. An empty list matches nothing. `ignoreCase: true` makes globs ignore case (`*.png` matches `LOGO.PNG`); regular expressions keep their own flags.

## `isFunction(value)`

A type guard for option schemas: `z.custom<Hook>(isFunction, 'Expected a function')` checks a callback without wrapping it.

## `isObject(value)`

A type guard for option schemas: a plain object, not `null`, an array or a class instance.

## `isRelativePathInside(value)`

For option schemas: a relative path that stays inside the folder it is relative to and is not that folder. `css/main.css` passes; `/tmp/x`, `../x` and `.` do not.

## `isUrl(value)`

Whether a path is a URL (`file://…`, `webpack://…`, `data:…`) rather than a file path. A Windows drive letter (`C:\x`) is not a URL.

## `toPosixPath(value)`

A path with `/` separators on every OS, for globs, archive entries, manifests and source maps.

## `toPluginError({ name, error, file? })`

Wraps anything in a `PluginError` prefixed with `name`, with `fileName` from the file; a `PluginError` is returned as it is. `createPlugin` uses it for every error.

## Types

* `FileHookInput` — `{ file: Vinyl }`, what a hook on a file receives; extend it for hooks with more keys.
* `ContentHookInput` — `FileHookInput & { content: string }`.
* `ContentHook` — `(input: ContentHookInput) => string | Promise<string>`, the hook on a file's text the plugins share.
* `RunContentHookInput`, `ApplySourceMapInput`, `AssertBinaryContentsInput`, `ParseOptionsInput`, `ToPluginErrorInput` — the inputs of the functions above.
* `SourceMap`, `BufferFile`, `PluginDefinition`, `BufferPluginDefinition`, `AnyPluginDefinition`, `PluginContext`, `TransformResult`, `PluginStream`.

## Re-exports

* `PluginError` — the class from [plugin-error](https://github.com/gulpjs/plugin-error).
* `Vinyl` — the file class from [vinyl](https://github.com/gulpjs/vinyl), and its type: `import type { Vinyl } from '@zilero/gulp-plugin-factory'`.

---
url: /gulp-plugins-hub/reference/testing.md
description: >-
  Test gulp plugins without gulp: createFile, runPlugin, getContents and
  getRelativePath from @zilero/gulp-plugin-factory/testing.
---

# Testing helpers

`@zilero/gulp-plugin-factory/testing` runs a plugin without gulp, for Vitest, Jest or `node:test`.

```ts
import { createFile, getContents, getRelativePath, runPlugin } from '@zilero/gulp-plugin-factory/testing';
```

## `createFile(input?)`

Creates a Vinyl file the way `gulp.src` would.

| Field       | Type                                                | Default      | Description                                                        |
| ----------- | --------------------------------------------------- | ------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `path`      | `string`                                            | `'file.txt'` | Path relative to `base`.                                           |
| `contents`  | `string \| Buffer \| NodeJS.ReadableStream \| null` | `''`         | A string is stored as UTF-8; `null` makes a file without contents. |
| `cwd`       | `string`                                            | `'/project'` |                                                                    |
| `base`      | `string`                                            | `<cwd>/src`  |                                                                    |
| `sourceMap` | `boolean`                                           | `false`      | Starts an empty map, like `src(…, { sourcemaps: true })`.          |

## `runPlugin(stream, files)`

Writes the files into the stream, ends it and resolves with every file it emitted, in order. Rejects with the first error the stream emits.

```ts
const output = await runPlugin(refilename({ suffix: '.min' }), [createFile({ path: 'app.js' })]);
```

## `getContents(file)`

The Buffer contents of an emitted file. Throws when the file is missing or has no Buffer contents, so tests need no casts or non-null assertions on `contents`.

## `getRelativePath(file)`

The file's path relative to its base with `/` separators, so a test compares the same string on Linux, macOS and Windows:

```ts
expect(output.map(getRelativePath)).toEqual(['js/app.min.js']);
```

## Types

`CreateFileInput`, the input of `createFile`.
